metadata.title: AI Architecture Advisor - Sources
metadata.description: Primary references for AI/ML architecture selection: gradient-boosted tree family, tabular foundation models (TabPFN-3 / TabICL v2), trees-vs-deep-learning on tabular data, older/foundational net families (RNN/LSTM, CNN/ViT, encoder-decoder/encoder-only, GAN/VAE), the prompt/reasoning/RAG/fine-tune decision, long-context-vs-RAG and RAFT, test-time compute / thinking budget, post-training & alignment (RLHF/PPO, DPO/DAAs, GRPO, RLVR, RLAIF/CAI), transfer learning/distillation, agent build-vs-not, MCP, SLMs for agents, model architecture (MoE granularity / attention variants MLA+NSA / SSM-hybrid / diffusion-LM), emerging classes (BLT, JEPA, world models), multimodal omni-vs-specialist, embedding/retrieval model selection, recsys/ranking, and how to discover & vet new architectures.

classical_ml_and_trees.name: XGBoost: A Scalable Tree Boosting System (Chen & Guestrin)
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Canonical XGBoost reference: regularization and second-order gradients.

classical_ml_and_trees.name: LightGBM: A Highly Efficient Gradient Boosting Decision Tree
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Histogram binning + leaf-wise growth; why LightGBM is fast on large data.

classical_ml_and_trees.name: CatBoost: unbiased boosting with categorical features
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Ordered boosting and native categorical handling; when CatBoost wins.

classical_ml_and_trees.name: Why do tree-based models still outperform deep learning on tabular data?
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Empirical basis for the trees-vs-deep-learning default on tabular data (2022; now contested for small tables by tabular foundation models).

classical_ml_and_trees.name: Accurate predictions on small data with a tabular foundation model (TabPFN v2, Nature 2025)
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: In-context tabular FM beats tuned GBDTs on datasets up to ~10k rows in a single forward pass; the 2025 update to 'trees always win on tabular'.

classical_ml_and_trees.name: TabPFN-2.5 / Prior Labs (state of tabular foundation models)
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Current tabular FM: when it beats tuned tree ensembles, size limits, and deployment tradeoffs vs GBDTs.

classical_ml_and_trees.name: TabPFN-2.5: Tabular Foundation Model (arXiv 2511.08667)
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Nov 2025 release raising the envelope to ~50k rows / ~2k features (~87% win-rate vs default XGBoost up to 100k rows) plus a distillation engine to compact MLPs/trees. Superseded by TabPFN-3 for size; kept for the distillation method. Volatile — verify limits.

classical_ml_and_trees.name: TabPFN-3 / Prior Labs (current tabular FM frontier)
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Released May 2026. Envelope is a rows-vs-features tradeoff, not a flat ceiling: up to 1M rows x 200 features, or 100K rows x 2K features, or 1K rows x 20K features. Licensed under the TABPFN-3.0 License v1.0 (permissive for research/internal evaluation; commercial/product use needs the API or a commercial license from Prior Labs, acquired by SAP in May 2026) — check before production. Volatile — verify limits (confirmed 2026-07-11).

classical_ml_and_trees.name: TabICL v2: open-source tabular foundation model (arXiv 2602.11139)
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Confirmed real: 'TabICLv2: A better, faster, scalable, and open tabular foundation model' (Qu, Holzmuller, Varoquaux, Le Morvan; submitted Feb 11 2026); open weights + inference code, reports beating RealTabPFN-2.5 without tuning/ensembling. The recommended alternative to TabPFN when its non-commercial license blocks deployment. Verify current benchmarks (confirmed 2026-07-11).

classical_ml_and_trees.name: scikit-learn: Ensemble methods (user guide)
classical_ml_and_trees.relevance: Bagging vs boosting, RandomForest and gradient boosting practical guidance.

foundational_net_families.name: Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch) — Sebastian Raschka (Manning, 2025)
foundational_net_families.relevance: End-to-end decoder-only LLM internals from first principles: BPE tokenization, self/causal/multi-head attention, layer norm, GELU, residuals, pretraining, SFT, and LoRA; the implementation anchor for the transformer/LLM and 'train from scratch' lanes (frames RNN/LSTM as the historical motivation for attention).

foundational_net_families.name: Long Short-Term Memory (Hochreiter & Schmidhuber)
foundational_net_families.relevance: The LSTM reference; still the right call for strict-streaming / tiny-footprint sequence models where Transformers are overkill.

foundational_net_families.name: Deep Residual Learning for Image Recognition (ResNet)
foundational_net_families.relevance: Canonical CNN reference; CNNs remain the default for spatial image features and edge/on-device vision before reaching for ViT at scale.

foundational_net_families.name: Exploring the Limits of Transfer Learning with a Unified Text-to-Text Transformer (T5)
foundational_net_families.relevance: Encoder-decoder (seq2seq) reference; the right shape for fixed text-to-text transforms (translate/summarize/parse) with paired data.

foundational_net_families.name: BERT: Pre-training of Deep Bidirectional Transformers
foundational_net_families.relevance: Encoder-only reference; still the default backbone for text classification/NER and the retrieval-embedding backbone behind RAG and rankers — not replaced by decoder-only LLMs.

llm_rag_finetune_decision.name: Retrieval-Augmented Generation for Knowledge-Intensive NLP (Lewis et al.)
llm_rag_finetune_decision.relevance: Foundational RAG reference; knowledge gaps via retrieval, not training.

llm_rag_finetune_decision.name: LoRA: Low-Rank Adaptation of Large Language Models
llm_rag_finetune_decision.relevance: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning; the practical adapt path for behavior gaps.

llm_rag_finetune_decision.name: RAFT: Adapting Language Model to Domain-Specific RAG
llm_rag_finetune_decision.relevance: Retrieval-augmented fine-tuning combines RAG grounding with behavior shaping instead of choosing one; the modern answer to RAG-vs-fine-tune as either/or.

llm_rag_finetune_decision.name: Long-Context LLMs Meet RAG: Overcoming Challenges for Long Inputs in RAG
llm_rag_finetune_decision.relevance: When long context obviates RAG vs when retrieval still wins; the long-context-vs-RAG decision the prompt->RAG ladder now must include.

llm_rag_finetune_decision.name: Anthropic: Building effective agents
llm_rag_finetune_decision.relevance: When a single call or workflow beats an agent; agent build-vs-not guidance.

llm_rag_finetune_decision.name: Model Context Protocol (MCP) specification
llm_rag_finetune_decision.relevance: The 2025 standard for agent tool/data integration; the protocol-choice consideration in the agent lane.

llm_rag_finetune_decision.name: Small Language Models are the Future of Agentic AI (NVIDIA)
llm_rag_finetune_decision.relevance: Argues SLMs are sufficient and cheaper for narrow, repetitive agent steps; reserve frontier models for hard planning.

reasoning_and_test_time_compute.name: The State of LLM Reasoning Model Inference (Raschka)
reasoning_and_test_time_compute.relevance: Survey of reasoning models and test-time compute; when scaling inference beats train-time fine-tuning for logic gaps.

reasoning_and_test_time_compute.name: Rethinking Fine-Tuning when Scaling Test-Time Compute
reasoning_and_test_time_compute.relevance: Test-time strategy interacts with fine-tuning choice; evidence the reasoning rung is distinct from the fine-tune rung.

transfer_and_distillation.name: Distilling the Knowledge in a Neural Network (Hinton et al.)
transfer_and_distillation.relevance: Teacher-to-student distillation: transfer behavior to a cheaper model.

transfer_and_distillation.name: A Survey on Transfer Learning (Pan & Yang)
transfer_and_distillation.relevance: Framework for choosing a knowledge-transfer mechanism by what stays fixed.

model_architectures.name: DeepSeek-V3 Technical Report
model_architectures.relevance: Foundational frontier MoE reference (671B total / 37B active); evidence MoE is the frontier default and where the dense-vs-MoE tradeoff (FLOPs vs VRAM) bites when self-hosting. Superseded on the frontier by DeepSeek-V4 (Pro 1.6T/49B active, Flash 284B/13B active; preview Apr 2026, 1M-token context) — cite V3 for the architecture rationale, V4 for current frontier scale. Verify current generation before quoting sizes.

model_architectures.name: Mamba: Linear-Time Sequence Modeling with Selective State Spaces
model_architectures.relevance: Foundational selective state-space model; basis for choosing SSMs over Transformers on long sequences / throughput.

model_architectures.name: Jamba: A Hybrid Transformer-Mamba Language Model (AI21)
model_architectures.relevance: Production-relevant SSM/attention hybrid with MoE; when KV-cache memory at very long context makes a hybrid beat a pure Transformer.

model_architectures.name: Mercury: Diffusion Large Language Models (Inception Labs)
model_architectures.relevance: Production diffusion-LM; Mercury 2 (Feb 2026) confirmed at ~1,000+ tok/s on current GPUs. Google's open diffusion-LM entrant is DiffusionGemma (Jun 2026, Apache-2.0, 26B MoE/3.8B active, 1000+ tok/s on H100) — distinct from the closed 'Gemini Diffusion' research demo (first shown May 2025, no public weights); name whichever is actually being proposed. Volatile — verify maturity and naming (confirmed 2026-07-11).

model_architectures.name: DeepSeek-V2 (Multi-head Latent Attention / MLA)
model_architectures.relevance: Introduces MLA: compresses the KV cache ~90%+ by projecting to a low-dim latent before caching; the standard attention variant on DeepSeek-class models and the key lever when KV-cache memory binds.

model_architectures.name: Native Sparse Attention (NSA, arXiv 2502.11089)
model_architectures.relevance: Hardware-aligned, natively-trainable block-sparse attention (compression + selection + sliding window); ~11x speedup at 64k context. Corrected 2026-07-11: NSA itself is the research precursor, not what shipped — DeepSeek-V3.2 (Sep 2025) runs the distinct, finer-grained DeepSeek Sparse Attention (DSA, via a lightning indexer), not NSA. Still the long-context cost lever to know when self-hosting; don't conflate the two.

model_architectures.name: GQA: Training Generalized Multi-Query Transformer Models
model_architectures.relevance: Grouped-query attention — the universal default attention variant in 2025-2026 open models; the baseline MLA/NSA improve on.

model_architectures.name: Byte Latent Transformer: Patches Scale Better Than Tokens (Meta)
model_architectures.relevance: Tokenizer-free byte-level architecture matching tokenized performance at scale; the leading emerging 'name but don't yet bet on it' alternative for robustness/multilingual.

post_training_and_alignment.name: Reinforcement Learning from Human Feedback (Nathan Lambert, 2026)
post_training_and_alignment.relevance: Comprehensive current treatment of the post-training/alignment stack: reward modeling (Bradley-Terry, ORM/PRM), PPO, GRPO/GSPO/CISPO, DPO and direct-alignment algorithms, rejection sampling, RLVR, RLAIF/Constitutional AI, over-optimization, and evaluation. The anchor reference for the post-training lane.

post_training_and_alignment.name: InstructGPT: Training LMs to follow instructions with human feedback
post_training_and_alignment.relevance: Canonical RLHF recipe (SFT -> reward model -> PPO); the historical baseline for the post-training lane.

post_training_and_alignment.name: Direct Preference Optimization (DPO)
post_training_and_alignment.relevance: Offline preference optimization without a reward model or RL loop; the default first preference-tuning method and basis for DAAs (KTO/ORPO/SimPO).

post_training_and_alignment.name: DeepSeek-R1: Incentivizing Reasoning Capability in LLMs via RL (GRPO)
post_training_and_alignment.relevance: GRPO + RLVR reasoning recipe (group-relative advantage drops the critic; verifiable rewards replace human labels); the widely-replicated 2026 reasoning-model training blueprint.

post_training_and_alignment.name: Tulu 3: Pushing Frontiers in Open Language Model Post-Training (AI2)
post_training_and_alignment.relevance: Open, reproducible end-to-end post-training recipe (SFT -> DPO -> RLVR); a canonical worked pipeline for the post-training lane.

post_training_and_alignment.name: Build a Reasoning Model (From Scratch) — Sebastian Raschka (Manning MEAP)
post_training_and_alignment.relevance: Reasoning-model build: inference-time compute scaling (CoT, voting, best-of-N), RL for reasoning (RLVR), and SFT+distillation; pairs the reasoning rung with implementation depth.

multimodal_and_embeddings.name: a16z: The State of Generative Media 2026
multimodal_and_embeddings.relevance: Evidence enterprises deploy many specialist models alongside omni models; the omni-vs-specialist multimodal decision. Verify figures before quoting.

multimodal_and_embeddings.name: MTEB: Massive Text Embedding Benchmark
multimodal_and_embeddings.relevance: Standard benchmark for comparing embedding models; the filter step in embedding-model selection (live leaderboard volatile — verify current leaders).

multimodal_and_embeddings.name: BGE-M3: Multi-Lingual, Multi-Functionality, Multi-Granularity Embeddings
multimodal_and_embeddings.relevance: Open-weight embedder with dense+sparse+multi-vector in one model; common self-hosted default and on-ramp to late-interaction retrieval.

multimodal_and_embeddings.name: ColBERT: Efficient Passage Search via Late Interaction over BERT
multimodal_and_embeddings.relevance: Late-interaction / multi-vector retrieval; when its precision justifies its storage cost in the retrieval-architecture axis.

recsys_and_ranking.name: Actions Speak Louder than Words: Generative Recommenders (Meta HSTU)
recsys_and_ranking.relevance: Production trillion-parameter generative/sequential recommender; evidence recsys is a distinct lane (implicit feedback, <50ms, dynamic catalog) not vector-RAG.

agents_and_context_engineering.name: Anthropic: How we built our multi-agent research system
agents_and_context_engineering.relevance: When multi-agent (orchestrator-worker) wins vs a single agent; token-cost multiples and parallel/independent-subtask conditions.

agents_and_context_engineering.name: Google Research: Towards a Science of Scaling Agent Systems
agents_and_context_engineering.relevance: Evidence multi-agent can lower quality on sequential tasks via coordination overhead; supports default-to-single-agent.

aws_and_document_services.name: Amazon Bedrock — model catalog and model cards
aws_and_document_services.relevance: AWS managed inference: Claude, Amazon Nova 2, OpenAI GPT-5.x, and 18+ providers / 110+ models available via Bedrock as of June 2026. The routing signal when 'must run on AWS' is the constraint.

aws_and_document_services.name: Amazon Bedrock Knowledge Bases
aws_and_document_services.relevance: AWS managed RAG path: S3 ingestion, built-in chunking + retrieval, zero-ops. Includes Amazon Nova 2 Multimodal Embeddings as the 2026 default embedder (supersedes Titan). Reach for this before building a custom RAG stack on AWS.

aws_and_document_services.name: Amazon Textract — developer guide
aws_and_document_services.relevance: AWS managed OCR specialist: structured extraction of forms, tables, and handwriting. The routing target when the multimodal specialist decision lands on AWS and OCR is the load-bearing capability.

aws_and_document_services.name: paperless-ngx — documentation
aws_and_document_services.relevance: Self-hosted OSS document store and OCR pipeline: REST API, IMAP/consume-folder ingestion, built-in OCR (Tesseract). The routing target when the specialist pipeline must be self-hosted and open-source.

aws_and_document_services.name: Amazon Bedrock Data Automation (BDA) — developer guide
aws_and_document_services.relevance: AWS-recommended default for intelligent document processing (IDP): FM-based classify and extract with flat per-doc pricing, with OCR-layer integration options alongside Textract for the extraction step. Route to Textract standalone only for high-volume standardized docs or 95%+ compliance SLA requirements. The specific 'Pipeline mode wraps Textract, March 2026' framing could not be re-confirmed against a dated primary source as of 2026-07-11 — verify the current BDA/Textract integration mechanics against the live developer guide before quoting a launch date.

aws_and_document_services.name: Amazon Kendra GenAI Index — developer guide
aws_and_document_services.relevance: Managed retriever index reusable across Amazon Q Business and Bedrock Knowledge Bases. Prefer over a per-surface KB when the same index must serve multiple surfaces (Q Business assistant + KB retrieval component simultaneously).

aws_and_document_services.name: Amazon Bedrock Rerank API — developer guide
aws_and_document_services.relevance: AWS native reranking: Cohere Rerank 3.5 and Amazon Rerank available via the Bedrock Rerank API. The managed quality lever for bi-encoder top-k → rerank top-n retrieval pipelines on AWS; reach for this before building a custom cross-encoder.

aws_and_document_services.name: Amazon Bedrock Guardrails — developer guide
aws_and_document_services.relevance: AWS-native safety and governance layer: content moderation, prompt-attack detection, denied topics, PII redaction, contextual grounding check (RAG faithfulness/hallucination gate with grounding + relevance thresholds), and Automated Reasoning (mathematically verifiable). Model-independent via the ApplyGuardrail API. The routing signal for regulated/safety-critical AWS deployments.

architecture_discovery_and_eval.name: LMArena (human-preference model leaderboard)
architecture_discovery_and_eval.relevance: Human-preference Elo across models; use as a directional elimination filter when discovering/vetting new models, not as a verdict.

architecture_discovery_and_eval.name: Hugging Face Daily Papers
architecture_discovery_and_eval.relevance: Primary release feed for scouting new architectures/methods; the discovery step before vetting.

architecture_discovery_and_eval.name: Artificial Analysis (model cost/intelligence/latency tracker)
architecture_discovery_and_eval.relevance: Cross-model cost vs quality vs latency tradeoff data for architecture/model selection and routing-policy design.

architecture_discovery_and_eval.name: V-JEPA 2: Self-Supervised Video Models / Joint-Embedding Predictive Architecture (Meta)
architecture_discovery_and_eval.relevance: Leading non-generative latent-predictive (JEPA) architecture; emerging-production for robotics/video understanding. The canonical example of the 'name but don't yet bet on it' emerging class for embodied/world-model work.
